relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: First project statement that copies attacker-controlled JSX child bytes into the parser buffer whose occupancy later reaches the full-buffer `p == q` state used by the vulnerable entity path.

Missing bounds check. `fxGetNextEntity()` assumes there is still payload room and writes `&` even when `p == q`, consuming the reserved terminator slot and advancing `p` past the end before the later `*p = 0` write. The fix wraps this store in `if (p < q)` and also skips `bsearch()` when nothing fit.
ASAN crash site. After the unguarded `&` write advances `p` to `q + 1`, this unconditional terminator store performs the observed 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow.

nodes.state: Immediately after the vulnerable `*p++ = "&";` executes at full-buffer state, `p` has advanced past `q`.

edges.evidence: vulnerable original: amp_write.p_after == entity_sink.p_for_nul == 0x631000010808 at ordered event indices 1 -> 2.

patch_resolves_note: The best-effort `switch-fixed --patch patch.diff` path failed because the staged checkout does not match the official fix context, so fixed-side evidence uses the authoritative `n132/arvo:49357-fix` image. There the original PoC reaches the same `fxGetNextEntity()` boundary state with `p == q`, but the guarded `&` store is skipped and the later `*p = 0` remains in-bounds; the adjacent case `drop_prev_amp_truncate_at_crash_amp` then provides the genuine witness where the fixed guard still allows the write with `p == q - 1`.
